chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:

No one should intercede regarding a hadd punishment once it has reached the Imam, for then he possesses authority over it. But intercede in a matter that has not reached the Imam if you see remorse; and intercede before the Imam in matters other than the hadd, with the approval of the one for whom intercession is made. And no intercession is to be made concerning the right of a Muslim man or anyone else except with his permission.

key_terms.النَّدَمَ: remorse indicating regret for the wrongdoing
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the legitimate authority or ruler overseeing judicial enforcement
key_terms.الْمَشْفُوعِ لَهُ: the person on whose behalf intercession is made
key_terms.حَدٍّ: a prescribed legal punishment under Islamic law
key_terms.حَقِّ: a legally recognized right or claim belonging to a person

ai.seo_question: When is intercession allowed or forbidden in hadd cases and personal rights according to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets limits on shafa'ah in judicial matters. It forbids intercession in a hadd case once it has formally reached the Imam, while permitting intercession before that stage when remorse is evident, and in non-hadd matters with the consent of the concerned person. It also affirms that the rights of individuals may not be negotiated through intercession without their permission.
